<b>Mindest-Laufzeit (Tagessoll):</b> hat:
Minimum runtime (daily target): if the device has not run that long by the bad-weather catch-up window, it is switched on there from the grid if needed until the target is met. Meant for water heaters and similar loads that have to be warm even after three rainy days. Requires automatic control – if it is off, there is no catch-up either.
Maximum runtime (daily limit): the counterpart – once the daily budget is used up, it stops until midnight. The limit stops automatic mode, schedules and catch-up alike (otherwise it would be useless for a pool pump); only a manual switch can still turn the device on. If the limit is below the daily target, the limit wins – the catch-up then stops there.
Both count the same runtime today – it restarts at zero every night (and after a restart) and only runs with a synchronised clock; with self-regulation only actual operation counts.

Der SolarLog liefert <b>Momentanwerte</b: The Solar-Log delivers instantaneous values – a single second that then stays on the dashboard until the next reading. A long interval therefore does not calm the display; it makes the jumps bigger and also slows down the control: evaluation only runs after a reading. Feste Programme, die das Gerät <b>unabhä:
Fixed programs that switch the device on regardless of the surplus – from the grid if necessary. For mandatory runtimes such as a pool pump: circulation has to happen whether the sun shines or not. Outside the programs everything stays as usual – if automatic mode is active, it may additionally switch the device on when there is a surplus.
If the end time is before the start time, the program runs past midnight (e.g. 22:00–06:00); the weekdays of the start day apply. A manual OFF pauses the running program until its end – it runs again the next day. During a program, neither fail-safe nor battery priority nor the time window apply – the maximum runtime/day does: once the daily budget is used up, the program rests until midnight.
Add programs with “Add program” and remove them with the ✕ in the row; more than four per device are not supported.
Fragt zusätzlich alle 15&nbsp;min die So: Additionally reads the Solar-Log objects 740/608/782 every 15 min (device list, status and power per inverter). With several inverters it also detects the failure of a single one – exactly the case that otherwise goes unnoticed for months.
Führt noch einmal durch Solar-Log, Steck: Walks through the Solar-Log, plugs and the network name once more. Existing settings are kept.
Für Geräte ohne eigenes Netzwerk-API – z: For devices without their own network API – e.g. a Tuya Bluetooth Fingerbot via Home Assistant. EnergyOptimizer only publishes an MQTT command here; a Home Assistant automation has to pass it on to the actual device.
Für Geräte, die <b>selbst entscheiden</b:
For devices that decide for themselves whether to run – dehumidifiers with a hygrostat, air conditioners, freezers. A plug that is on is then not runtime: if the humidity is below the value set on the device, it only draws standby power. Actual operation is detected from the measured power of the plug – above the run threshold the device counts as running. Only this time counts as operating hours and towards the minimum runtime/day. 0 = off (then “plug ON = running” applies as before).
A sensible run threshold lies between standby and operating power (dehumidifier: standby ~2–5 W, operation 200–500 W → e.g. 60 W). If the device stays without demand for longer than the second time, automatic mode releases the plug and only tries again 30 min later.
Für die Sonnenstandsberechnung. Erst wen: For the sun position calculation. Only when the sun is mathematically above 10° does 0 W production count as a fault – at dusk it is normal.

Sicherheitsabstand zum Netz. Eingeschalt: Safety margin towards the grid. A device is only switched on when the surplus covers its power plus the switch-on buffer – so a slightly underestimated device does not draw from the grid right away. It is switched off as soon as the deficit exceeds the switch-off buffer. The switch-off buffer should be larger than the switch-on buffer, otherwise the system oscillates. Larger values = more cautious, but less sun used.
